question:
Which of the following triads is NOT a Dobereiner’s triad?

(i) Li, Na, K

(ii) Ca, Sr, Ba

(iii) N, P, Sb

(iv) Cl, Br, I
solution:
The correct answer is __**only iii**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Dobereiner's Triads:** Johann Wolfgang Döbereiner was a German chemist who is best known for his work that led to the development of the periodic table. He identified groups of three elements (triads) that had similar properties and observed that the atomic weight of the middle element was approximately the average of the atomic weights of the other two elements.
 
• The triads mentioned in the options are as follows:
 
 
• (i) Li, Na, K
 
• (ii) Ca, Sr, Ba
 
• (iii) N, P, Sb
 
• (iv) Cl, Br, I
 
 
 
• **Explanation:**
 
 
• **Option (i): Li, Na, K** - This is a valid Dobereiner's triad as Lithium (Li), Sodium (Na), and Potassium (K) all belong to Group 1 (**Alkali metals**) and show similar properties.
 
• **Option (ii): Ca, Sr, Ba** - This is a valid Dobereiner's triad as Calcium (Ca), Strontium (Sr), and Barium (Ba) all belong to Group 2 (**Alkaline earth metals**) and show similar properties.
 
• **Option (iii): N, P, Sb** - This is NOT a valid Dobereiner's triad. Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), and Antimony (Sb) do not form a triad with similar properties and the atomic weight of P is not the average of N and Sb.
 
• **Option (iv): Cl, Br, I** - This is a valid Dobereiner's triad as Chlorine (Cl), Bromine (Br), and Iodine (I) all belong to Group 17 (**Halogens**) and show similar properties.
 
 
 
• **Conclusion:** Therefore, the triad that is NOT a Dobereiner's triad is Option (iii): N, P, Sb.
